key_insight: Video models may not be missing the correct physics—they may already encode it but fail to use it in generation. This paper shows that a low-dimensional intervention can recover and control the hidden, physically correct motion even when the model first outputs the wrong one.
problem_solved: It addresses the question of whether physically incorrect video generation is due to a model never learning the right motion, or due to the model learning it but not selecting it during generation.
method: Train a video model on a synthetic setting where red masses move slowly and blue masses move quickly.
Test the model on a conflict case where a red mass is observed moving fast, creating a mismatch between learned color-motion association and observed evidence.
Apply a low-dimensional causal edit to the model’s internal representation to redirect generation toward the correct motion.
impact: This suggests that failure modes in video generation may be fixable through targeted interventions rather than retraining. For practitioners, it opens a path toward controllable, interpretable, and more reliable video models.
visual_elements: Before/after diagram showing incorrect slow-motion output versus corrected fast-motion output
Simple causal graph or latent-space edit illustration
Color-coded motion timeline for red vs. blue masses
Model pipeline graphic highlighting where the low-dimensional intervention is applied
paper_title: A Chosen Future Can Still Be Rewritten: Causal Writability in Video Models
paper_authors: Xingyun Wang, Haomin Zheng, Man Yuan, Leqian Yang, Ziming Liu
